images.alt: The game CPU communicates through four byte ports with the sound CPU. The sound CPU and eight-voice DSP share 64KB of audio RAM containing a driver, samples and an echo buffer.
A schematic display has a window strip across its top and plane A below. The strip replaces that portion of plane A; plane B and sprites are combined separately through priority rules.
ANTIC fetches forty bytes for a normal high-resolution bitmap line. GTIA can interpret those 320 bits as eighty four-bit pixels, with modes choosing luminance, colour registers or hue.
The 6845 supplies memory and raster addresses, sync, display enable and cursor signals. External display circuitry fetches data and turns it into pixels and colour.
The C128 processor selects a VDC register through D600, waits for the ready status, then transfers data through D601. The VDC manages its own video RAM and generates the 80-column display.
An MML score passes through a parser or compiler, then a timed sound driver, then sound-chip registers. The text score and the hardware waveform are different stages.
A Smalltalk image contains objects, classes and development tools. A virtual machine executes its instructions, and a platform interface connects the system to the host computer.
The original wraparound cover names John Hardman and Andrew Hewson and lists the kinds of routines inside
De Re Atari cover with a parchment-style title and an Atari computer inside a circle, signed L. Cross ’81
Inside the Dragon cover showing a dragon above a Dragon computer and the names Duncan Smeed and Ian Sommerville
A note selects a keyboard-map entry, which chooses a sample; volume and panning envelopes shape the resulting voice
A library disk number leads to its contents record, which identifies the work, author, version, dependencies and distribution notes
A physical floppy leads to a raw capture, analysis and an IPF description of the data and its arrangement. Raw captures remain separate evidence.
ABABABAB can be described as AB followed by a six-byte copy from two bytes back. AAAAAAAA can be described as eight repetitions of A. These are concepts, not encoded Pucrunch bytes.
Object files and libraries feed a combined linking, arrangement and compression stage, which produces a Windows executable with startup code, a decoder and packed data.
One shared background supplies labels and a navigation button to three cards. Each card also has its own text and picture.
Film Strip supplies character pictures, Land Scape supplies level maps and Blue Print supplies Reptol behaviour definitions. File Link joins the saved pieces into a game file.
A top-down grid shows rays travelling from the player to walls. Nearby wall hits produce tall columns in the view; distant hits produce shorter columns.
A game event requests a change during a musical phrase. The score reaches an authored decision point, then takes a prepared transition into the next section.
The client displays predicted movement immediately. When an authoritative server state arrives, it starts from that state and replays movement commands the server has not yet accounted for.
World geometry receives a surface texture and a separate lightmap. The renderer combines surface detail and lighting to produce the visible wall.
